stem: A client reports persistent thirst and frequent passage of large amounts of very light-colored urine. Which disorder should the nurse suspect?

options.B: Syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion (SIADH)

rationale: The Endocrine Society describes diabetes insipidus as causing excessive thirst and frequent urination of large amounts of light-colored or clear urine. It occurs when antidiuretic hormone/vasopressin is insufficient or the kidneys do not respond appropriately to it. Therefore A is the best answer. SIADH is a water-retaining antidiuretic-hormone disorder rather than the characteristic polyuria pattern in the stem; primary aldosteronism and Cushing syndrome do not characteristically produce this combination of persistent thirst and large-volume dilute urination.
educational_objective: Recognize persistent thirst with frequent large-volume dilute urination as a characteristic presentation of diabetes insipidus.
source_locator: Opening definition and sections 'Endocrine Connection' and 'Diagnosis and Symptoms': excessive thirst; frequent urination of large amounts of light-colored/clear urine; central DI from insufficient ADH/vasopressin and nephrogenic DI from renal nonresponse
source_claim_supported: Diabetes insipidus causes excessive thirst and frequent passage of large amounts of clear/light-colored urine and can result from insufficient vasopressin/ADH or renal resistance to it.
